identity.narrative: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These source-owned handoffs do not establish full campaign, save, display or audio parity; Nexus and Theron's Quest remain explicitly bounded, with authentic level/campaign consumers still incomplete. The release also publishes Android and iOS arm64 artifacts; publication alone is not runtime verification. identity.narrative: General-purpose TypeScript C64 reverse-engineering toolkit controlling stock VICE and integrating disk/BASIC/static-analysis/assembly/equivalence workflows. package.json now declares 2.0.0 and publishable CLI/MCP/host bins, while the primary roadmap explicitly leaves npm trusted-publisher setup, the v2.0.0 tag and verification of the published package open. C64RT_TRACE adds per-process JSONL field traces for host requests, VICE lifecycle, MCP calls, native tool runs and stderr without exposing the trace to the agent. Node.js 24+, VICE 3.9+ and user-supplied ROMs remain prerequisites; no host CPU/RAM minimum or independent execution is established. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/11987768d056 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5ceac29bb61b Current M14 work now generates byte-identical ACME source from an unpacked image or PRG, curated knowledge and Ghidra instructions; an optional loader is run in VICE and checked at the recovered entry state. The documented ten-stage workflow adds explicit acceptance criteria, exit checks, deliverables and coverage reporting. Release comparison can attach first-access/runtime-change evidence to differing bytes, single-release separation reports unpack/access/reachability provenance, and platform symbols can be exported as an ACME include. These are upstream live-tool checks rather than an independent tracker run, and they do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/8e2bbb5a106c2fe339bc2f1aaaa8d02b414a1341 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/18bc1327744db353667cabf39d81ed373effe078 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/b80796c63719f7eeb4fd694afd689fe5a926cd8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/1c0070e068b719314a4ee47b56de189916b0a6d6 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/ad164faf2354087ee3c0f7bd8d9e52c36a367fbc M17 now captures CIA timer latches and interrupt masks that ordinary register reads cannot recover, programs generated loaders to restore the reachable timer state, and compares counters, latches, controls and masks at the entry jump. An upstream live test distinguishes the repaired loader from one without CIA restoration. The host also records each skill-script operation and outcome while keeping verbose MCP/VICE tracing opt-in. These are upstream tests; no local VICE run was performed, SID voice 3, TOD phase and interrupt flags remain documented limits, and the npm publication gate remains open. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5cdc74d5226db7d8123ca782cfb6e9a36a11ee8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/15a3bb8f331d0fe8d81976400c04a4e632813b06 M23/M24 now let execution traces continue while recording observations/history, generate linked source maps and program reference pages, and route evidence-producing agent run files into owned run directories. The Bruce Lee acceptance reports 70 reference pages, 1,227 entries, 21 decoded tables and deterministic second-pass linking; these are upstream field-run receipts and do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/4c209ab6e79cbb0a34e3b818bf33d8b6fb92f0ba https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/7a45b671dc7b6efc1f0c6b905e57ae1839a8ce3a https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/9caaff4bf206b429d389fcdf5e94d42919600cd9 v2.1.1 closes the previously open publication gate and reports a real-project field pass covering every script command and MCP tool on VICE 3.10. It hardens JAM state, snapshot failures, drive-side stops, static/provenance analysis and preflight validation; current main additionally rejects malformed media before VICE can reinterpret it, stops an in-flight autostart before snapshot restore and exposes the documented $A000-$BFFF VICE memory-map flaw. These are upstream field and regression receipts, not a tracker-side VICE run. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/releases/tag/v2.1.1 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/eb69c523cc34f88e9c2aa5e23f3139306ed6bb5b

identity.narrative: Identity: The primary README identifies REA as a CLI/MCP toolkit connecting agents to native, managed, JavaScript, firmware and runtime analysis providers. build.narrative: v0.0.43 publishes source and documents all exterior cells on CHIM plus collision/world-conversion fixes. No tracker-side conversion, build or gameplay test was performed, and the release is not promoted to complete playability. v0.0.46 restores per-region weather selection, the Ebonheart statue, third-person torch, Vivec walkway collision and Dreamer greetings; collision storage is reduced and NPC output is reported byte-identical across processor families. The release remains source-only and explicitly lists missing weather effects, doors, inventory work and other limitations.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The release publishes source and emulator-oriented project material but no new verified minimum physical CPU, RAM or OS profile. Existing 68040/FPU/AGA reference-target evidence remains qualified. The tagged FAQ identifies the current development baseline as A1200/AGA/PAL, 68040 with FPU, 2 MiB Chip RAM and 16 MiB additional Fast RAM. This is an accelerated emulator/reference contract, not proof of a physical minimum or acceptable real-hardware frame rate.

relationships.narrative: CHIM derives from AmiQuake with component-specific GPL terms; Morrowind assets are user-supplied and not relicensed. This is a native Amiga engine, not a generic emulator.

identity.narrative: Chip-oriented ST/Mega ST/STE/Mega STE emulator using Moira 68000 and comparing hardware behavior with Hatari. Its debugger exposes symbols, disassembly, breakpoints, watchpoints and headless operation. The README advertises desktop, web and Android packages; it explicitly says the Android APK was tested under QEMU but not on a real device. A large current-main change strengthens ST/STE and Mega STE hardware modeling, including SCC BREAK edge retention, in-flight MIDI divisor changes, IKBD BREAK resume, FDC live-media behavior and machine self-test paths. The commit documents ASan/UBSan regression counts and remaining approximations; it is not treated as universal compatibility proof or as a published release. identity.narrative: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27 Current main ports WinUAE's optional loopback GDB remote server, disabled by default and unavailable with the threaded CPU, with m68k registers, physical RAM/ROM, stepping, breakpoints, watchpoints and memory-map support. A separate MacPorts integration covers Apple Silicon and x86 hosts and explicitly credits ChatGPT for substantial assistance; this extends the AI record without implying whole-project generation. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/4faddbe399757a663fb3f2e8dc4be678eda96d4d https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/831f13e71ee6e872d6d3570f2c23068493d0dd15 Development head now honors database-requested 68040 AGA configurations, disables cycle-exact mode when requested, aligns Android previews with the launched CPU/FPU configuration and follows with 68030 database handling. IPC was redesigned to keep up to 16 clients across frames, bound per-frame work, cap requests at 64 KiB and queue replies without blocking the emulation thread. These guest CPU selections are emulated configurations, not Amiberry host target CPUs or minimum machines. No tracker-side WHDLoad or IPC run was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/5dc6c79f956b4a76b793cbc957242cb65345fed7 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/69b4be8173 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/2685d3e774cbdd3c99db0cee66aa6836642ed36c Development head ports WinUAE monitor extensions for AmigaDOS entry stops, Exec task controls, exceptions, DMA/range watchpoints, guest diagnostics, input, screenshots and frame checkpoints. Follow-up fixes bound replies, preserve resets, report checkpoint write failures and safely disassemble at memory-bank ends. This is source-level development evidence, not a new v8.4.0 release or an independent run. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/42335beeafe955c81df4dec31dd508867a6b3b4d Development head makes the local control interface available on Windows through account-scoped named pipes and exercises pipelining, stalled clients, size limits, abandoned connections, multi-instance endpoints and reply-before-quit on real headless emulator processes. Follow-up CPU work restores threaded-JIT block chaining, fixes stale interrupt and breakpoint handling, and prevents keyboard reset from racing a running CPU thread. These are source/CI receipts, not a new v8.4.0 artifact. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/caf799a4c7dc3c99f2b69ee4834e5f4a00a77aae https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/7dda88f302e74d38509a9ab0b37dfe79641cf8aa https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/e28372fec0e9a957bce3cf5e791db3e3931e1724

build.narrative: Current main adds Windows named-pipe IPC with behavioral CI and repairs threaded-JIT/reset correctness. These remain development-head results; the published baseline is v8.4.0 and no tracker-side run was performed. v8.4.2 publishes broad desktop/libretro assets and documents repaired threaded JIT/reset behavior, exact-SHA1 WHDBooter selection, monitor commands over GDB/IPC, WinUAE display corrections and expanded ZZ9000 services. The v8.4.2 release explicitly requires glibc 2.35 or newer for its x86-64 and ARM64 AppImages (Ubuntu 22.04 or later). Other published platforms still have no numeric minimum CPU/RAM evidence.

ai.narrative: Existing Claude and ChatGPT evidence remains; the keyboard-reset fix additionally has an explicit Copilot co-author trailer. Attribution is scoped to evidenced commits.

relationships.narrative: General-purpose Amiga machine emulator built on the UAE/WinUAE core, eligible as system emulation rather than a single-game emulator. Amiga is the emulated source machine, not a claim that the emulator runs natively on a classic Amiga. Host ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch claims do not redefine the guest CPU. Individual model/chipset/ROM combinations were not tested. GPL-3.0 source does not license external Kickstart ROMs, game disks or bundled third-party components. Repository metadata is not marked as a GitHub fork, but this does not erase explicit code/asset ancestry. Root-normalized dedup and prior-root screening passed the 1498-project baseline.

identity.narrative: Open-source Sharp MZ emulator with cycle-accurate Z80A execution, chip/peripheral emulation, a built-in debugger and an MCP bridge exposing screenshots, coverage, profiling and analysis controls. Primary docs provide Linux, Windows and macOS build paths; no minimum host CPU or RAM is stated. Claude client configuration documents a supported integration, not evidence that AI authored the project. Current main saves hidden Z80 MEMPTR, interrupt, EI-delay and T-state state plus CTC, scroll, VRAM-wait and floppy-controller state; it safely adapts RAMdisk/IDE8 snapshot loads. Debugger/MCP fixes expose all 532 expanded memory regions, keep debugger reads from firing guest watchpoints, correctly stop temporary run-to breakpoints and record the instruction bytes actually fetched by self-modifying code. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/1f477d90e2efd6808253c1c3d5f31fa56f465570 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/a5726b9658d10b4412cf4a28bc212a78351f28a4 Current main adds frame-boundary-synchronized memory search across user RAM, logical Z80 space, VRAM, extension banks, RAM disks and other writable memory, with numeric/string types, filters, undo/redo, candidate actions, freeze controls and write-origin inspection. Matching MCP tools expose searches and freezes for automation, and the same change fixes the missing second half of PEHU 512 KiB memory. A maintained locale catalog at the reviewed commit explicitly names Claude Code as Last-Translator, correcting the prior no-evidence AI audit while keeping attribution limited to that content. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78/src/locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/mz800emu.po

The new tests say the model matches all 129,504 measurements from the referenced GDG netlist simulation, with representative cases retained in-tree. This is upstream simulation/test evidence, not tracker-side execution.
